description: Mahasiswa Universitas Telkom dengan minat di AI, computer vision, dan analisis data. Untuk tantangan "Be An Earth System Trend Detective", saya ingin menganalisis data observasi bumi NASA untuk menemukan pola dan tren perubahan lingkungan. Saya mencari teman tim yang punya skill data analysis, data visualization, atau earth science.
summary: Earth System Trend Detective is a web tool that helps users investigate whether an Earth science variable is trending, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant. Users work with a time series exported from NASA Giovanni (for example, MERRA-2 2-meter air temperature averaged over a region). The tool converts it to annual means, plots the series with a trend line, and runs a Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope to report the direction, the rate of change per decade, and the p-value in plain language. Several regions can be compared side by side, because trends can differ between places. We demonstrate the tool with monthly MERRA-2 air temperature over the Bandung area (2001-2024), cross-checked and compared with NASA POWER data. It is designed for students and the public who want to become "data detectives" without writing statistical code.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Earth System Trend Detective answers the four questions of the challenge: what is changing, where, how much, and is the change statistically significant. It turns an Earth-science time series into a clear verdict in plain language.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data in: a NASA Giovanni time-series CSV (MERRA-2 M2TMNXSLV v5.12.4 monthly 2-meter air temperature, area-averaged over the Bandung area, 107.4E-107.8E, 7.1S-6.8S, 2001-2024). NASA POWER monthly data is used to compare other Indonesian cities and to cross-check the Giovanni file. Users can also upload their own Giovanni CSV for any variable and region.

2. Monthly values are averaged to annual means (years with less than 80% coverage are dropped), which removes the seasonal cycle.

3. A Mann-Kendall test checks for a linear trend and Sen's slope measures its size.

4. Results: change per decade, total change, p-value, "significant / not significant", and a plain-language sentence. Non-significant trends are still reported, as the challenge encourages.

FEATURES

Trend lines, place-to-place comparison, annual anomaly charts, a month-by-year anomaly heatmap, a validation view (Giovanni CSV vs NASA POWER) and a trend map.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Students and members of the public can act as "data detectives" without writing statistical code. Comparing places shows that trends can differ from one region to another, even when the same process drives them.

TOOLS

Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Altair, PyDeck. Data: NASA Giovanni, MERRA-2, NASA POWER.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

We chose robust, widely used climate statistics (non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope, which do not assume normally distributed data and resist outliers). We added a validation view and state its limits openly.

LIMITATIONS

Only linear trends on annual means are tested. The Bandung series is a regional average from Giovanni, while other cities are single NASA POWER grid points. NASA POWER meteorology is derived from MERRA-2, so the validation view checks consistency, not independent confirmation.

LINKS

Live app: https://earth-system-trend-detective.streamlit.app/

Source code: https://github.com/tissuedry/earth-system-trend-detective

USE OF AI

The code was developed with the assistance of an AI tool (Claude, Anthropic) and reviewed and run by the team. This is also stated in the README and the code header.
dataRefs: MERRA-2 M2TMNXSLV v5.12.4 (2-meter air temperature, monthly)
